statement.p: Use the linear approximation to estimate
Compare with the value given by a calculator and compute the percentage error:

static.solution:
(-0.98)^{2}(-2.99)^{2} is a value of the function f(x,y)=x^{2}y^{2}.
We use the linear approximation at the point (-1,-3), which is f(-1+h,-3+k) \approx f(-1,-3)+f_x(-1,-3)h+f_y(-1,-3)k We compute the value of the function and its partial derivatives at (-1,-3): \left. \begin{array}{lcl} f(x,y)=x^{2}y^{2} \amp \amp f(-1,-3)=9 \\ f_x(x,y)=2xy^{2} \amp \Rightarrow \amp f_x(-1,-3)=-18 \\ f_y(x,y)=2x^{2}y \amp \amp f_y(-1,-3)=-6 \end{array} \right.
Substituting these values gives the approximation
f(-1+h,-3+k)\approx 9-\left(18h+6k\right) We substitute h=0.02, k=0.01 to obtain (-0.98)^{2}(-2.99)^{2} \approx 8.58 The absolute value of the actual value given by calculator is |f(-0.98,-2.99)|\approx 8.58607.
The error is 0.00607204 and the percentage error is \frac{0.00607204}{8.58607}\times 100\%=0.0707196 \%
